outcome.technical: Retry of attempt 1, built on its work in the task tree. ITEM 1: tools/lints/_deps.py STATE_WRITERS gains a row for scripts/governance/drive-phase.py set_aside_tree (a redo moves a whole worktree directory; git worktree move refuses a tree with a submodule checked out, a file writer cannot move a directory). Seen red first: tests/test__deps.py --selftest -> 253/254, sw1 FAIL naming 'line 5013: os.rename in set_aside_tree()'; after the row 254/254, state_write_violations() -> []. ITEM 2 (MED): drive-phase.py set_aside_tree (:4983) now records the move under the drive-state key asideMoves ({from, admin, record}) together with the keptTrees entry, THEN locks git's record of the tree (_lock_for_move :4873, `git worktree lock --reason ASIDE_LOCK`), then rewrites the marker, then renames (:5034). The lock is given back only by _finish_aside (:4911) after _repair_moved_tree succeeds; _unlock_moved (:4882) removes a lock only when the record's `locked` file carries the drive's own ASIDE_LOCK reason, so a lock someone else placed is never taken off. A failed lock, marker write or rename takes the set-aside back (_take_back_aside :4920: marker restored, own lock removed, entries dropped) and the stop says whatever of that did not hold. A failed repair stops via aside_unread (:4974), naming `git worktree repair <aside>`, record still locked. repair_asides (:4937) runs first in drive_locked (:8946), i.e. at the start of every drive step: a move still recorded is repaired again and unlocked (did-line), a move that never happened (tree still at its path) is taken back, and a tree at neither path stops the drive. Verified against the reviewer's pA.py on the fixed tree: prune -v printed nothing, the admin dir survived, and git refused the task-add-like add ('is a missing but locked worktree'). pD.py renames by hand without calling set_aside_tree, so it cannot exercise the fix; ta11b covers add -f through the real path. ITEM 3 (low): the rename-failure path now reports a failed marker restore (write_record's why), and _repoint_module (:4833, split out of _repair_moved_tree) catches UnicodeDecodeError and ValueError (undecodable core.worktree; os.path.relpath across Windows drives) into a reason. ITEM 4 docstrings: remove_task_tree now says 'no submodule checked out, at whatever commit, no link directory holding a file' and 'IGNORED FILES ARE NOT ASKED AFTER AND GO WITH THE TREE'; recut_tree's opening now says the old tree is not taken down to make room, and that the one remover takes it down later, ignored files included, only when it holds nothing else; tree_undescribed says a removal deletes every ignored file whatever wrote it, no longer that the setup can make them again; set_aside_tree keeps 'nothing the old one holds is lost' now that the lock holds the record across the move. The lock reason is a literal constant because the suite's argv prose lint (mt2/mt3) refuses a built string after a --reason flag; where the tree goes lives in the drive state. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the set-aside paragraph now describes the lock, asideMoves, the repeated repair and take-back, with case ids; the ignored-files sentence was corrected. TESTS (ta-block, now 25 cases): ta1c (the set-aside of ta1 is listed at its new path, unlocked; over-fire twin), ta11 (a stubbed repair failure leaves the record locked, `git worktree prune -n -v` prints nothing, admin/modules stands, the stop names git worktree repair <aside>), ta11b (git worktree add -f at the task path is refused), ta11c (the next step repairs: listed at the aside path, unlocked, prune names nothing, the submodule reads there), ta12 (failed rename + failed marker restore -> the stop names the restore failure and the key), ta12b (record left unlocked after a failed rename; twin), ta13 (undecodable core.worktree -> a reason, not an exception), ta13b (relpath ValueError -> a reason), ta14 (a run that died after the lock and marker but before the move is taken back by repair_asides), ta14b (a record a human locked is not set aside and their lock stays), ta14c (a recorded move over that record is taken back without removing their lock). Red before the fix, with only the tests changed (`python3 tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage ta-block` -> 16/22): ta11, ta11b, ta11c, ta12, ta13, ta13b FAIL. ta1c and ta12b passed by construction (twins). ta14, ta14b and ta14c were written after the reorder, so their red is the probe's (L1, L6, L7) and the submit helper's at HEAD. outcome.descriptive: A redo's set-aside tree now keeps git's record of it locked from before the move until git reads it at its new path, and a failed repair is retried on the next step, so no prune or forced add can take the tree's index, marker or submodule repositories.
